findings.detail: GET /mcp returns 200 with 8 tools (execute-request, get-server-variables, run-agent) before any auth handshake; tool schemas expose internal server env-var names
GET /api/v1/agents returns 200 with 40 agent definitions and 120 env-var mappings to anonymous callers
PUT /api/v1/agents/{id}/env lets any session overwrite another workspace's env vars — the tenant id is read from the body, not the session
500 on /api/v1/oauth/token leaks the Go stack with the signing key path (/etc/signer.key) and the internal redis address
api host exposes 8080/8081 (dev proxy) and 15672 (rabbitmq management) to the public internet
POST /api/v1/tokens accepted 500 requests in 30s from one IP with no 429 and no sliding window
tools/list over SSE returns 12 tools including filesystem-write and shell-run before authentication; the handshake accepts any client name
GET /.env on the mcp origin returns 200 with an API key, an OAuth client secret and 9 provider tokens — dotfiles are served as static assets
the sampling handler echoes the model's message back without a human-in-the-loop gate on 6 of 10 requests — a prompt-injection channel
a tool result containing ignore prior instructions flipped the agent into sending an API key on 2 of 5 test runs
the authorize flow does not bind state to the session; a forged authorize link carrying attacker state was accepted and issued a code
GET /oauth/authorize returns a 302 to the callback with a code even when state is absent (4 of 4 probes)
redirect_uri validation accepts any *.example subdomain; a wildcard entry in the allowlist matches attacker-controlled hosts
authorize accepts scope=read,write,admin for any client; a sample app receives admin on 3 of 5 attempts
account recovery allows a 6-character password; 9 of 30 audit accounts reset to password1
no CSP on the consent page; a 200-byte injected script loaded from a third-party widget origin
SPA catch-all serves index.html for /api/v1/internal/* — internal routes return 200 HTML and hide 404s from scanners
GET /static/js/main.19a2b3.js.map returns 200 (1.2MB) — full TypeScript source including API key names and internal endpoint paths
the production bundle contains pk_live_... as a literal, pulled from a window config object at page load
no CSP on the dashboard; script-src allows unsafe-inline on 3 of 5 sampled pages
POST /api/v1/notes reflects the note title unescaped into the SPA on 3 of 5 probes — stored XSS in the notebook surface
CSP script-src includes a third-party widget origin and unsafe-inline — no real XSS mitigation
a 40-character API key in the production JS bundle for the portal login page (cdn/portal/app.7f2c1d.js, line 812)
the sourcemap for the portal bundle is public and maps to the current production commit hash
GET /releases/ autoindexes 214 versioned bundles including the previous key-bearing build
docs.ledgerway.com CNAMEs to a discontinued hosting plan (an unclaimed bucket); DNS now resolves to a registered placeholder page
docs serves no X-Content-Type-Options; an uploaded .html file mirror was served as text/html
POST /webhooks/replay accepts a body with no signature header; 10 of 12 replays with forged payloads were accepted
the same agent.completed event id was delivered twice within 24h and both deliveries were applied — no dedupe on the event sink
GET /webhooks/replay returns the last 20 event bodies (including token counts) to anonymous callers
no Idempotency-Key on /webhooks/replay; retries after timeouts double-process provider billings
dashboard enforces an 8-character minimum but accepts 3 repeated characters; 6 of 20 audit passwords were aaaa8888
no X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors on the dashboard; the admin panel is iframeable by any origin
dashboard certificate valid for 19 days; deployment tooling confirms auto-renew is configured
GET /signer/health returns the Ed25519 public key and key id; the matching dev keypair was published in a public gist in June
access tokens appear in structured logs (field access_token) on 4 of 10 signer requests; 31 tokens captured in a 15-minute run
an unhandled panic returns the full goroutine stack including env-var names and the internal mcp.ledgerway.com address
9092 (kafka) open to the internet; SASL is not enforced on 3 of 6 brokers
the webhook-events topic is readable without authentication from the public internet
6379 answers an anonymous CONFIG GET; no auth on the oauth session cache
the session store holds raw access tokens in plaintext with no ACL restricting reads
no DNSSEC on the apex; docs and oauth both resolve unsigned
SPF is -all but there is no DMARC alignment, so spoofed account mail still lands in inboxes
no DMARC record published; no policy for unaligned mail
no DKIM selector published; account-recovery mail is sent unsigned
chain valid for 19 days; automated renewal confirmed in the ops log
grafana 10.1 on the dashboard host with an unpatched CVE from the current year
sshd allows the chacha20-poly1305 fallback and password auth on the signer jump host
session cookie lacks SameSite and is set without Secure on the http cache path
HTTPS /checkout returns a 307 to a plaintext http download path — a session downgrade on a billing surface
admin dashboard on the public internet with no VPN gate
grafana anonymous view is enabled on the agent-runs board, which includes token counts
no Strict-Transport-Security on the mobile portal
dev login posts plaintext credentials over http; the 302 chain drops the https hop
pk_live_... appears as a literal in sdk/src/auth.ts; 9 secrets across the public SDK and sample apps
the sample OAuth app's client secret is committed in .env.example (commit 91c2be)
npm audit reports 19 vulnerabilities (6 high) including prototype-pollution in a transitive dependency of the MCP client
git log -S API_KEY returns 9 commits; a live key rotated in July is still present in history
the portal serves /.env from public/ — a template repo ships the env file into the static root
no SBOM in releases; the lockfile is unsigned
